controls.name: kind
controls.doc: The compressor's character, which picks its detector: `comp` runs the RMS detector, `limiter` the peak detector. The console's comp row carries it (`CompState.kind`, `COMP_KINDS`) and comes up as `comp`.

controls.name: detectorOversampling
controls.doc: The compressor's detector oversampling: `auto` runs the control path at 4x only while the attack is faster than DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_AUTO_MS, `off` never, `4x` always (omx-dsp's OMX_DYN_OVS_AUTO, _OFF and _X4, in that order, so the index mapping holds). The ids are the console's wire vocabulary (`CompState.detectorOversampling`, what the dynamics row's OPTIONS publishes and a session stores), so the console re-exports this set; it comes up `auto`.

controls.name: detectorTopology
controls.doc: Where the compressor's detector listens: `feedforward` hears the slot's input (or its key), `feedback` hears the slot's own pre-make-up output DYN_FB_LOOP_DELAY_SAMPLES late, through one envelope stage, and a keyed slot stays feed-forward (omx-dsp's OMX_DYN_TOPOLOGY_FEEDFORWARD 0 and _FEEDBACK 1, in that order; the set is named for its control, so C spells them OMX_DETECTOR_TOPOLOGY_*). The console's comp row carries it (`detectorTopology`) and comes up `feedforward`, so a zeroed atom is the compressor every slot runs.

controls.name: keySource
controls.doc: Where the compressor's detector listens: its own input (self), or the key handed to its sidechain port (sidechain), in the order of the integer the key port carries; the gate's keySource ids. Which strip or bus feeds the sidechain is console routing. It comes up self.

controls.name: keyHpHz
controls.doc: The key filter's high-pass corner, Hz: the gate's key filter (one Butterworth section, in double), on what the detector hears and never on the audio. 0 is out, the come-up value, and the compressor is the one without it, bit for bit.

controls.name: keyLpHz
controls.doc: The key filter's low-pass corner, Hz, after the high-pass. 0 is out, the come-up value.

controls.name: keyTiltDb
controls.doc: The key's tilt, in dB per octave at KEY_TILT_PIVOT_HZ: positive brightens what the detector hears, negative darkens it (omx_tilt, a first-order shelf pair about the pivot, after the key filter). 0 is flat, the come-up value, bit for bit.

controls.name: keyListen
controls.doc: While on, the output is what the detector hears, the key after its filter and tilt, folded as detectLink folds it: linked the two legs, mid the mid on both, side the side on both, max the mid on the left and the side on the right. The compressor keeps running underneath. It comes up off.

controls.name: holdMs
controls.doc: The hold, ms: the detector is frozen this long after its level last rose, so the reduction holds before the release runs. 0 is no hold, the come-up value.

controls.name: detectLink
controls.doc: How the detector folds the key's two legs into one level, in the order of the integer the kernel reads: linked, the louder leg (the compressor's own detection, the come-up value); mid, the mid (L + R)/2; side, the side (L - R)/2; max, the louder of the mid and the side. One gain serves both legs whatever the fold.

controls.name: duck
controls.doc: The ducker: on, the reduction the key's level asks for is held to rangeDb, so the programme gain is max(rangeDb, the compressor's law at the key's level). It comes up off.

controls.name: rangeDb
controls.doc: The ducker's depth, dB: the deepest the programme goes while the key is above the threshold. 0 ducks nothing. Read only while duck is on.

controls.name: releaseMode
controls.doc: How the compressor releases, in the order of the integer the kernel reads: `fixed`, the detector's release at releaseMs, the compressor that shipped bit for bit and the come-up value; `opto`, the program-dependent release of PROGRAM_RELEASE_PROFILES.opto (an LA-2A's two-stage recovery, slower the longer the cell was driven); `auto`, the same word with PROGRAM_RELEASE_PROFILES.auto (a bus compressor's AUTO position). In opto and auto the detector releases at its attack pole and releaseMs is inert, kept for when fixed returns (omx_env_program_release on the gain, after the gain computer).

readouts.name: gainReductionDb
readouts.doc: The compressor's gain reduction, in dB with CLAP's sign: 0 while it reduces nothing, negative the reduction it applies. The display range runs down to COMP_LIMITS.thresholdDb.min: on a signal at or below 0 dBFS the reduction (x - T)(1 - 1/R) never exceeds -T, and T is at least the threshold's minimum.

readouts.name: keyLevelDb
readouts.doc: The level the compressor's detector reads now, dBFS: the key after its filter, tilt and fold while one is set, the programme's louder leg otherwise. The display range is the threshold's travel, so the meter and the threshold share one axis.

readouts.name: effectiveAttackMs
readouts.doc: The attack the detector runs, ms: attackMs, but in the feedback topology where the loop's pole is floored at (ratio - 1)/ratio so it cannot ring (omx_dyn_fb_attack_pole), the time constant of that floor at the running rate, -1000/(rate ln((R - 1)/R)). It equals attackMs whenever the floor is not reached.

COMP_LIMITS.doc: The legal range of each compressor field (engineering units). The widget clamps drags to these, `normalizeComp` enforces them, the row's codec refuses by them and the travel sheet publishes them. `default`/`defaultFrom` are the come-up values `defaultCompState` seeds a fresh strip with, read BACK from here rather than restated there.

PROGRAM_RELEASE.doc: The program-dependent release's model constants — the LA-2A's opto cell as DATA. `chargeMs`/`dischargeMs` are the word's memory constants, shared by every profile; each profile's `fastMs`, `slowMinMs`, `slowMaxMs` and `share` fit the unit's published two-stage recovery (opto); `auto` spans a bus compressor's fixed release detents, 100 ms to 1.2 s, half fast and half slow, provisional until a published figure refits it. Not operator controls: generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_PROGRAM_RELEASE_*`, which libomxdsp's `omx_env_program_release` reads.

DYN_FB_LOOP_DELAY_SAMPLES.doc: The feedback detector's loop delay, in samples: the output y[n] depends on the gain at n, so the detector can only have heard y[n - 1]. Not a latency: the audio is never delayed by it. omx-dsp's feedback state holds exactly this many output samples per leg.

DETECTOR_OVERSAMPLE_LATENCY_SAMPLES.doc: What the 4x detector oversampling costs the strip it is engaged on, in samples: the causal linear-phase half-band's reach, by which the audio is delayed so the gain still lands on the sample it was computed from. A sample count, not a time: the same at every rate. omx-dsp's oversampler declares the same number as OMX_OVS_LATENCY_4X, and its comp and gate faces report it while 4x is engaged.

KEY_TILT_PIVOT_HZ.doc: Where a key's tilt pivots, Hz: the frequency a tilt leaves at unity while it brightens or darkens what the detector hears. One pivot for every key that tilts.
